iterations.theme: Životni put mons. Vlade Košića: od djetinjstva i svećeničkog poziva, preko iskustva rata i biskupske službe, do obnove biskupije i ljubavi prema Gospi

sections.subtitle: Muževi s krunicom kao znak vremena: Marija kao „ruka spasa”
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Vlado Košić govori o katoličkim muževima koji javno mole krunicu
sections.content:
Epizoda otvara jednom od najsnažnijih misli cijelog razgovora. Sisački biskup **mons. Vlado Košić** govori o pokretu muževa koji se okupljaju kako bi javno molili krunicu. Ističe da to nije samo hrvatska pojava: muževi su se već i drugdje okupljali kako bi upravo molitvom krunice svjedočili svoju vjeru.

U tome biskup vidi jasan znak. Prema njegovim riječima, *odgovorni katolički muževi* vide kako svijet „srlja u propast” i u Mariji prepoznaju „ruku spasa”. Tom rečenicom najavljena je tema na koju se razgovor kasnije vraća, ali prije toga voditelj gosta vodi kroz cijeli njegov životni put.
sections.subtitle_en: Men with the Rosary as a sign of the times: Mary as a "hand of salvation"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mons. Vlado Košić speaks about Catholic men who publicly pray the Rosary
sections.content_en:
The episode opens with one of the most powerful thoughts of the entire conversation. The Bishop of Sisak **Mons. Vlado Košić** speaks about the movement of men who gather to pray the Rosary publicly. He emphasizes that this is not only a Croatian phenomenon: men have already gathered elsewhere as well to witness their faith precisely through the prayer of the Rosary.

In this, the bishop sees a clear sign. According to his words, *responsible Catholic men* see how the world is "rushing into ruin" and recognize in Mary a "hand of salvation". With that sentence, the topic to which the conversation later returns is announced, but before that, the host leads the guest through his entire life path.

sections.subtitle: S Kaptola na Veliki Kaptol: šaljiv uvod u razgovor sa sisačkim biskupom
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup se smije dok objašnjava razliku između zagrebačkog Kaptola i sisačkog Velikog i Malog Kaptola
sections.content:
Voditelj podcasta *Redefinicija* goste pozdravlja riječima „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip” te predstavlja monsinjora Vladu Košića, biskupa sisačkog. Uvodni razgovor je opušten. Voditelj pita je li bila gužva, a biskup priznaje da jest i da je studio „jedva našao”.

Zatim voditelj šaljivo pita gdje je jednostavnije biti, u Velikom ili u Malom Kaptolu. Biskup Košić objašnjava da Sisak ima i Mali i Veliki Kaptol, dok Zagreb ima „samo Kaptol”. Zato se znao šaliti kako je **„došao s Kaptola u Veliki Kaptol”**. Što se prometa tiče, dodaje, Sisak je jednostavniji, dok su gužve u Zagrebu „nekada gotovo jedva svladive”. Voditelj se slaže da nije lako živjeti u velikom gradu, ali zahvaljuje Bogu što su se upravo u Zagrebu susreli.
sections.subtitle_en: From Kaptol to Veliki Kaptol: a humorous introduction to a conversation with the Bishop of Sisak
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop laughs while explaining the difference between Zagreb's Kaptol and Sisak's Veliki and Mali Kaptol
sections.content_en:
The host of the *Redefinicija* podcast greets the guests with the words "Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph" and introduces Monsignor Vlado Košić, Bishop of Sisak. The introductory conversation is relaxed. The host asks if there was traffic, and the bishop admits that there was and that he "barely found" the studio.

Then the host jokingly asks where it is simpler to be, in Veliki or in Mali Kaptol. Bishop Košić explains that Sisak has both Mali and Veliki Kaptol, while Zagreb has "only Kaptol". That is why he used to joke that he **"came from Kaptol to Veliki Kaptol"**. As far as traffic is concerned, he adds, Sisak is simpler, while traffic jams in Zagreb are "sometimes almost barely manageable". The host agrees that it is not easy to live in a big city, but thanks God that they met right in Zagreb.

sections.subtitle: Od Družbinca do Šalate: sretno djetinjstvo okruženo s četiri naraštaja
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić prisjeća se rodnog Varaždina i obiteljskog doma u Družbincu
sections.content:
Na pitanje o prvim uspomenama biskup Košić kreće od početka. Rođen je u **Varaždinu**, a za sebe kaže da je „Varaždinec, domovine sin”. Odrastao je u obiteljskom domu u **Družbincu**, u župi **Petrijanec**. Ondje je kršten, primio prvu pričest i krizmu, a kasnije ondje slavio i mladu misu. U Petrijancu je završio i osam razreda osnovne škole.

Njegov se školski i formacijski put može sažeti ovako:
- **osnovna škola** u Petrijancu,
- **sjemenište na Šalati** u Zagrebu,
- nakon mature **vojni rok u Rumi**,
- zatim **bogoslovija na Kaptolu** u Zagrebu.

Djetinjstvo opisuje kao lijepo i sretno. Odrastao je uz roditelje i sestru, ali i uz djeda i baku, pa čak i uz pradjeda i prabaku, kojih se i danas sjeća. Selo pamti kao „prozračno”, puno životinja i prirode. Prijelaz u grad bio mu je nešto teži, no ondje se posvetio knjizi. Volio je čitati i učiti, a zajedno s kolegama u sjemeništu bavio se i sportom i glazbom. Zaključuje kako „može reći da je njegovo djetinjstvo bilo sretno”.
sections.subtitle_en: From Družbinec to Šalata: a happy childhood surrounded by four generations
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić recalls his native Varaždin and the family home in Družbinec
sections.content_en:
When asked about his first memories, Bishop Košić starts from the beginning. He was born in **Varaždin**, and says of himself that he is „a native of Varaždin, son of the homeland”. He grew up in the family home in **Družbinec**, in the parish of **Petrijanec**. There he was baptized, received first Communion and confirmation, and later celebrated his first Mass there as well. In Petrijanec he also completed eight grades of elementary school.

His educational and formation path can be summarized as follows:
- **elementary school** in Petrijanec,
- **seminary at Šalata** in Zagreb,
- after graduation **military service in Ruma**,
- then **theological seminary at Kaptol** in Zagreb.

He describes his childhood as beautiful and happy. He grew up with his parents and sister, but also with his grandfather and grandmother, and even with his great-grandfather and great-grandmother, whom he still remembers today. He remembers the village as „airy”, full of animals and nature. The transition to the city was somewhat harder for him, but there he devoted himself to books. He loved to read and study, and together with his peers in the seminary he also engaged in sports and music. He concludes that „he can say that his childhood was happy”.

sections.subtitle: Zašto se ne čuje varaždinski naglasak: biskup o standardnom jeziku
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o važnosti standardnog hrvatskog jezika i pravilnih naglasaka u javnom govoru
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da se kod gosta ne osjeti varaždinski naglasak i da je teško pogoditi odakle je. Biskup Košić objašnjava da je to plod truda. Njegovi učitelji, i u osnovnoj školi u Petrijancu i u srednjoj školi u Zagrebu, imali su jasan stav da učenici trebaju usvojiti **standardni hrvatski književni jezik**, s pravilnim naglascima i razlikovanjem *č* i *ć*.

Priznaje da se danas zavičajni govor tolerira, pa čak i potiče, i smatra da je to lijepo. Ipak, drži da javne osobe svakako trebaju znati standardni jezik. Drago mu je kad ljudi ne mogu pogoditi otkud je, pa ga pitaju je li iz Slavonije. Uz smijeh dodaje da se ipak čuje da nije iz Dalmacije.

Ne skriva ni da mu u javnosti smetaju „ružni naglasci, baš na prvi slog”. Zbog toga se, kaže, ljuti, „ali što si mogu pomoći, nitko mene ne pita”.
sections.subtitle_en: Why the Varaždin accent cannot be heard: the bishop on the standard language
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about the importance of the standard Croatian language and proper accents in public speech
sections.content_en:
The host notes that the Varaždin accent cannot be felt in the guest and that it is difficult to guess where he is from. Bishop Košić explains that this is the fruit of effort. His teachers, both in elementary school in Petrijanec and in high school in Zagreb, had a clear stance that students should adopt the **standard Croatian literary language**, with proper accents and the distinction between *č* and *ć*.

He admits that today native regional speech is tolerated, and even encouraged, and he considers that to be nice. Still, he holds that public figures certainly ought to know the standard language. He is glad when people cannot guess where he is from, so they ask him whether he is from Slavonija. With a laugh, he adds that it can still be heard that he is not from Dalmacija.

Nor does he hide that in public he is bothered by "ugly accents, right on the first syllable". Because of that, he says, he gets angry, "but what can I do, nobody asks me".

sections.subtitle: Ispit iz latinskog i proročanstvo župnika: „Ti buš župnik!”
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup prepričava kako je kao dječak položio ministrantski ispit iz latinskog
sections.content:
Na pitanje kako je razlučio svećenički poziv, biskup Košić najprije govori o obitelji. Bila je to **pobožna obitelj** koja je zajedno molila kod kuće i redovito išla na misu. Župnik ih je rado posjećivao, iako inače nije bio otvoren za mnogo susreta s vjernicima. Razlog je bio težak: partizani su mu ubili brata na kućnom pragu, a htjeli su ubiti i njega. Onima kod kojih je dolazio, međutim, bio je prijatelj i imao je povjerenja u njih, a jedna od tih obitelji bila je i Košićeva.

Malog Vladu fasciniralo je kako se oko župnika okupljaju ministranti, pa je i sam htio ministrirati. Prepreka je bio ispit iz latinskog. Bilo je to oko 1969. ili 1970., kad je pohađao četvrti razred. Od četvorice dječaka jedan je slomio ruku, pa je pouka prekinuta. Vlado nije odustao. Poručio je preko zvonara župniku da je „sve naučio”, iako latinske odgovore, priznaje, nije razumio. Župnik ga je ispitao i pustio, a dječak je **trčao kući i skakao od veselja** jer je postao ministrant.

Obitelj je njegovu želju podupirala. Biskup se prisjeća i pokojnog kapucina **fra Ilije Boraka**, koji ga je jednom upitao: „Vlado, buš kapucin?”, a on je odgovorio: „Bum.” Ipak, župnik **Antun Posavec** imao je drukčiji plan. Rekao mu je da neće biti ni kapucin ni isusovac, kojih je upoznao na trodnevnom susretu ministranata na Šalati, nego: „**Ti buš župnik.**” Mali Vlado inače je govorio da će biti „ili župnik ili poljoprivrednik”. Odabrao je prvo i nakon osnovne škole otišao na Šalatu.
sections.subtitle_en: The Latin Exam and the Pastor's Prophecy: "You'll Be a Pastor!"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop recounts how, as a boy, he passed the altar server Latin exam
sections.content_en:
To the question of how he discerned his priestly vocation, Bishop Košić speaks first about his family. It was a **pious family** that prayed together at home and regularly went to Mass. The pastor gladly visited them, although he was not otherwise open to many encounters with parishioners. The reason was difficult: the Partisans had killed his brother on his doorstep, and they wanted to kill him as well. To those whose homes he visited, however, he was a friend and had trust in them, and one of those families was the Košić family.

Little Vlado was fascinated by how altar servers gathered around the pastor, so he wanted to serve at the altar himself. The obstacle was the Latin exam. It was around 1969 or 1970, when he was attending fourth grade. Of the four boys, one broke his arm, so the instruction was interrupted. Vlado did not give up. He sent word to the pastor through the bell ringer that he had "learned everything," although, he admits, he did not understand the Latin responses. The pastor examined him and passed him, and the boy **ran home and jumped for joy** because he had become an altar server.

The family supported his desire. The bishop also recalls the late Capuchin **fra Ilija Borak**, who once asked him: "Vlado, will you be a Capuchin?", and he answered: "I will." Nevertheless, the pastor **Antun Posavec** had a different plan. He told him that he would be neither a Capuchin nor a Jesuit, whom he had met at a three-day gathering of altar servers on Šalata, but rather: "**You'll be a pastor.**" Little Vlado otherwise used to say that he would be "either a pastor or a farmer." He chose the former and after elementary school went to Šalata.

sections.subtitle: Generacija '78.: prijateljstva koja traju gotovo pola stoljeća
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o godišnjim susretima maturanata generacije 1978.
sections.content:
Na Šalati se, kaže, pronašao. Imao je dobre ocjene, cijenili su ga poglavari i profesori, a dobro se slagao i s kolegama. Ta se prijateljstva njeguju i danas. Maturanti **generacije '78.** sastaju se svake godine, a za dvije godine slavit će **50 godina mature**.

Susreti su se održavali na raznim mjestima. Posljednji je bio u Dragancu kod Čazme, prethodni u Sračincu kod Varaždina, a biskup je dvaput bio domaćin u Sisku. Za 50. obljetnicu, ako Bog da, kolege će ponovno pozvati k sebi. U generaciji su i oni koji su se ostvarili u civilnom i obiteljskom životu, a petnaestak ih je postalo svećenicima. Susreti uvijek imaju isti tijek: sveta misa, ručak, razgovor i zajedničko fotografiranje. Povezuje ih i zajednička skupina na WhatsAppu.

Posebne veze ima i s generacijom zaređenom **1985.**, kada je i sam postao svećenik. I s njima slavi obljetnice.
sections.subtitle_en: Generation of '78: friendships that last almost half a century
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about the annual meetings of high school graduates of the generation of 1978.
sections.content_en:
At Šalata, he says, he found himself. He had good grades, superiors and professors appreciated him, and he got along well with his classmates too. Those friendships are nurtured even today. High school graduates of the **generation of '78** meet every year, and in two years they will celebrate **50 years of graduation**.

The meetings were held in various places. The last one was in Draganac near Čazma, the previous one in Sračinec near Varaždin, and the bishop hosted twice in Sisak. For the 50th anniversary, God willing, he will invite his classmates to his place again. In the generation there are also those who realized themselves in civil and family life, and about fifteen of them became priests. The meetings always follow the same course: Holy Mass, lunch, conversation, and taking photos together. They are also connected by a shared group on WhatsApp.

He also has special bonds with the generation ordained in **1985**, when he himself became a priest. With them, too, he celebrates anniversaries.

sections.subtitle: Od Dubovca do Hrastovice: župa koju je rat razorio
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup opisuje izbijanje rata i progonstvo svoje župe u Hrastovici
sections.content:
Nakon ređenja Vlado Košić bio je tri godine kapelan u **Karlovcu na Dubovcu**, a zatim dvije godine u **Španskom u Zagrebu**. Nakon pet godina kapelanske službe dobio je svoju prvu župu, **Hrastovicu kod Petrinje**. Bilo je to 1990., godinu dana prije rata.

Ljude u Hrastovici brzo je zavolio, a oni njega. Zajedno su pokrenuli mnoge duhovne i materijalne inicijative. U rat, priznaje, isprva nije vjerovao: „Kakav rat, to su se neke tri budale napile.” Ipak, sukob je eskalirao. Župa je morala bježati, svi su bili prognani, a bilo je i poginulih. Mladi župnik obilazio je ljude, tješio ih i pokapao svoje poginule.

Prisjeća se početaka hrvatske vojske, tadašnjeg ZNG-a, i nemoći branitelja. Kad je zarobljeni **Đuro Vranečan** u snimci preko radija upitan je li se u crkvi dijelilo oružje, nasmijao se i odgovorio da je kod crkve imao „stražu sa štapom”. „Nismo se imali čime braniti, a oni su imali”, zaključuje biskup.

Opisuje i razmjere razaranja. Okupirano je bilo sve južno od Kupe i Save, a ondje se nalazilo **14 župa**, uz kapele, župne kuće i samostane. „Sve porušeno, sve su uništili”, kaže, jer je cilj bio da nestane „sve što je katoličko” na tom području. Najviše je stradalo 1991., ali razaranje je trajalo sve do oslobođenja 1995.
sections.subtitle_en: From Dubovac to Hrastovica: a parish destroyed by war
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop describes the outbreak of the war and the exile of his parish in Hrastovica
sections.content_en:
After ordination, Vlado Košić was an assistant priest for three years in **Karlovac on Dubovac**, and then for two years in **Špansko in Zagreb**. After five years of service as an assistant priest, he received his first parish, **Hrastovica near Petrinja**. It was in 1990, a year before the war.

He quickly grew fond of the people in Hrastovica, and they of him. Together they launched many spiritual and material initiatives. In the war, he admits, he did not believe at first: „What war, some three fools just got drunk.” Nevertheless, the conflict escalated. The parish had to flee, everyone was exiled, and there were also casualties. The young parish priest visited the people, comforted them, and buried his fallen.

He recalls the beginnings of the Croatian army, the then ZNG, and the helplessness of the defenders. When the captured **Đuro Vranečan** was asked in a radio recording whether weapons were being distributed in the church, he laughed and answered that by the church he had a „guard with a stick”. „We had nothing to defend ourselves with, and they had,” concludes the bishop.

He also describes the scale of destruction. Everything south of the Kupa and Sava was occupied, and **14 parishes** were located there, along with chapels, parish houses, and monasteries. „Everything demolished, they destroyed everything,” he says, because the goal was for „everything that is Catholic” in that area to disappear. The most suffered in 1991, but the destruction lasted all the way until liberation in 1995.

sections.subtitle: Tri godine na prvoj crti: barake, vreće s pijeskom i vjeronauk
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o životu uz kapelu Svetog Jakova u Mošćenici tijekom rata
sections.content:
Nakon progonstva boravio je s kolegama u Petrinji, zatim u Maloj Gorici, a najduže u Selima. Tada ga je **kardinal Kuharić** imenovao župnikom Petrinje, iako sama Petrinja nije bila dostupna. Pod kontrolom je ostala samo kapela u **Mošćenici**, selu između Siska i Petrinje.

Ondje je postavio drvenu baraku, a vjernici su, kako sam naglašava, obnovili kapelu **Svetog Jakova**. Uz nju je proživio **tri godine na prvoj crti**. Vodio je Caritas i brinuo se za ljude. Kako je u školi bilo više stotina djece, nije ni pomišljao na odlazak: „Zašto bih ja bježao ako su djeca tu?” Predavao je vjeronauk u toj školi i u gimnaziji u Sisku.

Prisjeća se slike koju bi danas „teško netko zamislio”: **vreće s pijeskom na prozorima**, jer je svakog trena mogla pasti granata. „Ali smo se ipak držali, nismo se dali i izdržali smo do kraja”, kaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Three years on the front line: barracks, sandbags, and religious education
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about life beside the Chapel of Saint James in Mošćenica during the war
sections.content_en:
After the exile, he stayed with colleagues in Petrinja, then in Mala Gorica, and longest in Sela. At that time, **Cardinal Kuharić** appointed him pastor of Petrinja, even though Petrinja itself was not accessible. Only the chapel in **Mošćenica**, a village between Sisak and Petrinja, remained under control.

There he set up a wooden barrack, and the faithful, as he himself emphasizes, restored the Chapel of **Saint James**. Beside it, he spent **three years on the front line**. He led Caritas and cared for the people. As there were several hundred children in the school, he did not even think about leaving: „Why would I flee if the children are here?” He taught religious education in that school and at the gymnasium in Sisak.

He recalls an image that today „someone could hardly imagine”: **sandbags on the windows**, because a shell could fall at any moment. „Yet we held on, we did not give up, and we endured until the end,” he says.

sections.subtitle: Iz pastoralne službe na fakultet i najmlađi biskup u HBK-u
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup navodi da je danas najstariji biskup po ređenju u HBK-u
sections.content:
Godine 1995. izabran je za asistenta na **Katoličkom bogoslovnom fakultetu**. Dvije godine bio je asistent, a nakon doktorata viši asistent. Na katedri dogmatske teologije predavao je četiri do pet dogmatskih traktata, a predavao je i na Katehetskom institutu. Nastavnik na KBF-u ostao je sve do 2005.

U međuvremenu, **6. veljače 1999.**, zaređen je za zagrebačkog pomoćnog biskupa, zajedno s biskupom **Josipom Mrzljakom**. Zato je danas, kaže, **najstariji biskup po ređenju u HBK-u**. U Zagrebu je bio pomoćni biskup jedanaest godina, a u Sisku mu teče sedamnaesta godina službe.
sections.subtitle_en: From pastoral service to faculty and the youngest bishop in the HBK
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop states that today he is the oldest bishop by ordination in the HBK
sections.content_en:
In 1995, he was elected as an assistant at the **Catholic Faculty of Theology**. For two years he was an assistant, and after his doctorate a senior assistant. At the department of dogmatic theology, he taught four to five dogmatic treatises, and he also taught at the Catechetical Institute. He remained a lecturer at KBF until 2005.

In the meantime, on **February 6, 1999**, he was ordained an auxiliary bishop of Zagreb, together with Bishop **Josip Mrzljak**. That is why today, he says, he is **the oldest bishop by ordination in the HBK**. In Zagreb, he was an auxiliary bishop for eleven years, and in Sisak he is in his seventeenth year of service.

sections.subtitle: Noć uoči „Oluje”: slalom između tenkova s maticama u autu
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup prepričava noć kad su tenkovi stigli do kapele u Mošćenici uoči oslobođenja
sections.content:
Voditelj se vraća ratnim godinama, koje je biskup opisao u knjizi ***Župnik na prvoj crti***, i preporučuje je svima. Podsjeća i na detalj da su biskup i njegova kuharica dan prije oslobođenja mogli izgubiti život.

Biskup objašnjava da su vojnici akciju držali u tajnosti, iako su mu obećali da će ga upozoriti. Ipak je osjećao da se nešto sprema. Noć prije napada **tenkovi su stigli do same kapele u Mošćenici**. Izašao je i upitao kreću li u oslobađanje. Kad su potvrdili, rekao je da bi se onda bilo bolje maknuti, a oni su se složili.

U auto je spremio knjige i **župne matice** i krenuo „kao u nekom slalomu između tenkova” prema Zagrebu. Na putu od Siska prema Selima, oko pet sati ujutro, čuo je početak kanonade, artiljerijsku pripremu za oslobađanje Banovine. „Bogu hvala, to se brzo riješilo”, kaže, „ali je zapravo jako velika cijena.”
sections.subtitle_en: The night before "Storm": slalom between tanks with parish registers in the car
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop recounts the night when tanks arrived at the chapel in Mošćenica on the eve of the liberation
sections.content_en:
The host returns to the war years, which the bishop described in the book ***Župnik na prvoj crti***, and recommends it to everyone. He also recalls the detail that the bishop and his cook could have lost their lives the day before the liberation.

The bishop explains that the soldiers kept the operation secret, even though they had promised him they would warn him. Still, he felt that something was brewing. The night before the attack, **the tanks reached the very chapel in Mošćenica**. He went out and asked if they were setting off to liberate. When they confirmed, he said that it would then be better to move away, and they agreed.

He packed the books and **parish registers** into the car and set off "as if in some slalom between the tanks" toward Zagreb. On the way from Sisak toward Sela, around five o'clock in the morning, he heard the beginning of the cannonade, the artillery preparation for the liberation of Banovina. "Thank God, that was resolved quickly," he says, "but it was actually a very high price."

sections.subtitle: Cijena slobode: priča o zapovjedniku Predragu Matanoviću
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup emotivno govori o poginulom zapovjedniku Predragu Matanoviću
sections.content:
Kao primjer te cijene biskup navodi **Predraga Matanovića**, kojega opisuje i u knjizi. Vjenčao ga je s njegovom **Natalijom** u kapeli Svetog Jakova, a poslije ga je i pokopao. Natalija je na sprovodu bila u visokoj trudnoći. „Ružna, teška situacija”, kaže biskup.

Matanović je bio hrabar čovjek. Bazu je imao u vojarni u Lađarskoj ulici u Sisku, gdje su bili **Gromovi**. Suborci su ga cijenili i voljeli jer je kao pirotehničar znao proći kroz minska polja, ući neprijatelju u zaleđe i točno znati gdje se tko nalazi.

Biskup ipak naglašava da „nisu bile dobre komande”. Kasnije analize pokazale su da je napad iz Mošćenice prema Petrinji bio taktički krivo postavljen, pa su poginuli mnogi. Za dan-dva smjer je promijenjen: vojska je preko pontonskog mosta kod **Letovanića prema Nebojanu** ušla u zaleđe Petrinje, na cestu prema Glini. Kad su se našli opkoljeni, neprijatelji su pobjegli prema Dvoru i Petrinja je oslobođena.

S obiteljima poginulih branitelja i civila biskup je povezan i danas, iako su neki roditelji u međuvremenu preminuli. „Upisao sam se u živote tih ljudi i oni u moj život”, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Price of Freedom: The Story of Commander Predrag Matanović
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks emotionally about the fallen commander Predrag Matanović
sections.content_en:
As an example of that price, the bishop mentions **Predrag Matanović**, whom he also describes in the book. He married him to his **Natalija** in the Chapel of Saint James, and later he also buried him. Natalija was heavily pregnant at the funeral. "An ugly, difficult situation," the bishop says.

Matanović was a brave man. His base was in the barracks on Lađarska Street in Sisak, where the **Gromovi** were stationed. His fellow fighters respected and loved him because, as a combat engineer, he knew how to navigate minefields, enter the enemy's rear, and know exactly where everyone was positioned.

The bishop nevertheless emphasizes that "the commands were not good." Later analyses showed that the attack from Mošćenica toward Petrinja was tactically flawed, leading to many deaths. Within a day or two, the direction was changed: via the pontoon bridge at **Letovanić toward Nebojan**, the army entered the rear of Petrinja, onto the road toward Glina. When they found themselves surrounded, the enemy fled toward Dvor and Petrinja was liberated.

The bishop remains connected with the families of fallen defenders and civilians to this day, even though some parents have passed away in the meantime. "I became inscribed into the lives of those people, and they into mine," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Biskup s 39 godina: imenovanje koje je obitelj dočekala „jaukanjem”
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o iznenađenju zbog imenovanja i o tome da je bio najmlađi biskup
sections.content:
Na pitanje je li očekivao biskupsko imenovanje, biskup Košić odgovara da nije. Iznenađenje je bio već izbor za asistenta na fakultetu. Kad ga je **profesor Golub** pitao bi li se prijavio na natječaj, odgovorio je da je deset godina nakon diplome već „prestar” i da u ratu nije stigao studiozno raditi. Golub mu je savjetovao da se pomoli i, ako želi, prijavi. Prijavio se misleći da ga neće izabrati. Od trojice kandidata dvojica su bila doktori znanosti, a on magistar, no profesori su izabrali njega. Morao je ostaviti župu, ali, kaže, vjernike nikad zapravo nije ostavio.

Imenovan je **29. prosinca 1998.**, a zaređen **6. veljače 1999.** u zagrebačkoj katedrali. Imao je tada oko 39 i pol godina, pa je bio vjerojatno među najmlađim biskupima u Europi. **Nadbiskup Bozanić** ispričao mu je da su mu iz Rima prigovorili kako je kandidat premlad. Bozanić je odgovorio da je i sam u toj dobi postao biskup, i to ordinarij, krčki biskup. Biskup Mrzljak sve je sažeo riječima: „Obećali smo poslušnost.”

Iza smiješnih scena krila se teška borba. „Bio sam jako potresen i bilo mi je jako teško”, priznaje. Kad je novinar *Glasa Koncila* **Miklenić** došao razgovarati s njegovom obitelji, ukućani su govorili: „To je teško Vladi sada.” Prema biskupovim riječima, „više su jaukali nego slavili”. Službu je prihvatio kao **križ** i nosi ga, kaže, do danas.
sections.subtitle_en: A bishop at 39: an appointment that the family greeted with „wailing”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about the surprise regarding the appointment and about being the youngest bishop
sections.content_en:
To the question of whether he expected the episcopal appointment, Bishop Košić answers that he did not. Even the selection as an assistant at the faculty was a surprise. When **Professor Golub** asked him if he would apply for the competition, he replied that ten years after graduation he was already „too old” and that during the war he did not manage to work studiously. Golub advised him to pray and, if he wished, apply. He applied thinking they would not select him. Of the three candidates, two held doctoral degrees and he held a master's, but the professors chose him. He had to leave the parish, but, he says, he never actually left the faithful.

He was appointed on **December 29, 1998**, and ordained on **February 6, 1999**, in the Zagreb Cathedral. He was around 39 and a half years old at the time, so he was probably among the youngest bishops in Europe. **Archbishop Bozanić** recounted to him that objections had come from Rome that the candidate was too young. Bozanić replied that he himself had become a bishop at that age, and an ordinary at that, the Bishop of Krk. Bishop Mrzljak summarized everything with the words: „We promised obedience.”

Behind the funny scenes lay a difficult struggle. „I was very shaken and it was very hard for me,” he admits. When *Glas Koncila* journalist **Miklenić** came to speak with his family, the household members said: „It is hard for Vlado now.” According to the bishop's words, „they wailed more than they celebrated.” He accepted the ministry as a **cross** and carries it, he says, to this day.

sections.subtitle: Rođenje Sisačke biskupije: radost unatoč „misijskom” teretu
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup objašnjava zašto se radovao osnivanju Sisačke biskupije
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što je bilo teže: postati biskup ili preuzeti novu, obnovljenu biskupiju s mnogo posla. Biskup bez dvojbe odgovara da je teže bilo postati biskup. Kardinal ih je obavijestio da ih je papa već imenovao. Odbiti se moglo samo zbog vrlo ozbiljnih razloga, uz dokaze ili liječničke potvrde, pa su, kaže, bili „dovedeni pred gotov čin”.

Osnivanju **Sisačke biskupije** se, naprotiv, radovao. Poznavao je taj kraj i njegove ljude, a i oni su poznavali njega. Prisjeća se kako je **pater Bonaventura Duda**, kad mu je spomenuo da se radi na osnivanju biskupije, rekao: „**To će biti misijska biskupija.**”
sections.subtitle_en: The Birth of the Diocese of Sisak: Joy Despite the “Missionary” Burden
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop explains why he rejoiced at the establishment of the Diocese of Sisak
sections.content_en:
The host asks what was more difficult: becoming a bishop or taking over a new, renewed diocese with a lot of work. The bishop answers without hesitation that it was more difficult to become a bishop. The cardinal informed them that the pope had already appointed them. Refusal was possible only for very serious reasons, with evidence or medical certificates, so, he says, they were “presented with a fait accompli”.

At the establishment of the **Diocese of Sisak**, on the contrary, he rejoiced. He knew that region and its people, and they also knew him. He recalls how **pater Bonaventura Duda**, when he mentioned to him that work was being done on the establishment of the diocese, said: “**That will be a missionary diocese.**”

sections.subtitle: Mučenička biskupija i predziđe kršćanstva
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o svetom Kvirinu i pojmu antemurale christianitatis
sections.content:
Biskup Košić Sisačku biskupiju naziva **mučeničkom**. Kroz povijest su ondje ljudi stalno ginuli: od turskih osvajanja, preko partizanskih zločina i protjerivanja, do Domovinskog rata, a na kraju je došao i potres. Kao najzorniji primjer navodi **Zrin**, župu koja je potpuno uništena: ljudi su pobijeni i protjerani, a sve je porušeno.

Zaštitnik biskupije je **sveti Kvirin**, sisački biskup i mučenik. Biskup ističe da je to područje bilo **predziđe kršćanstva**, *antemurale christianitatis*. Taj je izraz upotrijebio **papa Lav X.** u pismu iz 1509. upućenom **Petru Berislaviću** nakon njegove pobjede nad Turcima kod Dubice.

Naglašava da pritom nije riječ samo o obrani Zapada ili Europe. Hrvati su kao vjernici branili kršćanstvo, jer su tada „kršćanstvo i Europa” bili isto. Ta kršćanska Europa, kaže, danas više ne postoji, ali na ta područja i dalje „navaljuju i nasrću”, a mučeništvo traje. „Bogu hvala, još smo tu”, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: A Diocesan Martyrdom and Bulwark of Christianity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about Saint Quirinus and the concept of antemurale christianitatis
sections.content_en:
Bishop Košić calls the Diocese of Sisak a **martyred** one. Throughout history, people were constantly dying there: from the Turkish conquests, through Partisan crimes and expulsions, to the Homeland War, and finally an earthquake arrived as well. As the clearest example, he cites **Zrin**, a parish that was completely destroyed: the people were slaughtered and expelled, and everything was demolished.

The patron saint of the diocese is **Saint Quirinus**, Bishop of Sisak and martyr. The bishop points out that this area was the **bulwark of Christianity**, *antemurale christianitatis*. That term was used by **Pope Leo X** in a 1509 letter sent to **Petar Berislavić** after his victory over the Turks near Dubica.

He emphasizes that it is not merely about defending the West or Europe. As believers, Croats defended Christianity, because at that time "Christianity and Europe" were the same. That Christian Europe, he says, no longer exists today, but upon those areas they continue to "assail and attack," and the martyrdom endures. "Thanks be to God, we are still here," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Biskup graditelj: dvostruko više srušenih crkava nego u ratu
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup iznosi brojke o obnovi 52 crkvena objekta nakon potresa
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na biskupovu izjavu da će ga jednog dana zvati **biskupom graditeljem**. Biskup Košić potvrđuje da je to „zapalo” njega. Nakon Domovinskog rata ostala je *terra combusta*, spaljena zemlja, ali je do njegova dolaska u Sisak 2010. većina crkava već bila obnovljena. Ostale su tri: u Gori, u Hrvatskoj Kostajnici i u Maloj Solini. Na njima je počeo raditi, a onda je došao potres.

Brojke koje navodi govore same za sebe:
- **52 crkvena objekta** u obnovi ili izgradnji,
- od toga **28 župnih crkava**, dvostruko više od 14 stradalih u ratu,
- 14 do 15 kapela koje su spomenici kulture,
- pet do šest župnih kuća, dva samostana i crkveni muzej,
- **16 objekata završeno**, još četiri mogla bi biti gotova ove godine, a 30 se intenzivno obnavlja.

Obnova ide preko biskupije, a biskup osobno nadzire radove i potpisuje ugovore. Poznaje projektante, statičare i izvođače, od kojih pet-šest tvrtki radi dobro. Investitor je **Ministarstvo kulture**, a prvi dio financirao je **Fond solidarnosti Europske unije**. Danas gotovo svaki mjesec otvara i blagoslivlja po jednu crkvu.

Nakon potresa od **29. prosinca 2020.** biskupija je već 2021. nabavila **14 montažnih dvorana**, pa su vjernici tih župa mogli slaviti euharistiju. Ostale su se župe snalazile u župnim i društvenim dvoranama. Uz osmijeh dodaje da je nekima sada žao napustiti dvorane, jer su ondje imali grijanje i klimu, a nova crkva, „makar lijepa”, zna biti hladna. Procjenjuje da će obnova trajati još dvije do tri godine. Voditelj dodaje da biskup ne gradi samo crkve, nego i vjerničku zajednicu, a biskup skromno odgovara: „Pokušavam.”
sections.subtitle_en: Bishop the builder: twice as many destroyed churches as in the war
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop presents figures on the renewal of 52 church buildings after the earthquake
sections.content_en:
The host recalls the bishop's statement that one day he would be called the **bishop the builder**. Bishop Košić confirms that this "fell to" him. After the Homeland War, what remained was *terra combusta*, scorched earth, but by his arrival in Sisak in 2010, most of the churches had already been restored. Three remained: in Gora, in Hrvatska Kostajnica, and in Mala Solina. He began working on them, and then the earthquake struck.

The figures he cites speak for themselves:
- **52 church buildings** under renewal or construction,
- of those, **28 parish churches**, twice as many as the 14 damaged in the war,
- 14 to 15 chapels that are cultural monuments,
- five to six parish houses, two monasteries, and a church museum,
- **16 buildings completed**, another four could be finished this year, and 30 are undergoing intensive renewal.

The renewal is carried out through the diocese, and the bishop personally oversees the work and signs the contracts. He knows the designers, structural engineers, and contractors, among whom five to six companies work well. The investor is the **Ministry of Culture**, and the first part was financed by the **European Union Solidarity Fund**. Today, almost every month, he opens and blesses one church.

After the earthquake of **December 29, 2020**, the diocese had already in 2021 procured **14 prefabricated halls**, so the faithful of those parishes were able to celebrate the Eucharist. Other parishes managed in parish and community halls. With a smile, he adds that some are now sorry to leave the halls, because they had heating and air conditioning there, while the new church, "however beautiful", can be cold. He estimates that the renewal will last another two to three years. The host adds that the bishop is not only building churches, but also the community of believers, and the bishop modestly replies: "I try."

sections.subtitle: Mamine pjesme o Gospi i petnaest godina na čelu mariološkog instituta
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o pjesmama svoje majke o Blaženoj Djevici Mariji
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je biskup predavao mariologiju, pisao knjige i pjesme o Mariji te organizirao simpozije i izdavanje zbornika. Pita ga koliko mu je Marija važna. „Ona je meni jako draga i veoma važna”, odgovara biskup. Odrastao je uz **majčine pjesme o Blaženoj Djevici**, koje mu i danas „odzvanjaju u uhu i srcu”. Kao dijete volio je svibanjske i listopadske pobožnosti, a to se, kaže, „otisne čovjeku u dušu”.

Član je **Hrvatskog mariološkog instituta**, a bio mu je i predsjednik. Naslijedio je **profesora Rebića**, koji je institut vodio 25 godina, a sam ga je vodio 15 godina. Nakon njega deset je godina na čelu bio **Ivan Karlić**. Sada je u tijeku prijelazno razdoblje u kojem se statut usklađuje sa statutom KBF-a.

Institut je organizirao **tuzemne simpozije** koji su istraživali mariološku baštinu pojedinih biskupija, pa je jedan održan i u Sisku, a drugi u Dubrovniku, Splitu i Đakovačko-osječkoj nadbiskupiji. Članovi su zapaženo sudjelovali i na **međunarodnim kongresima**: tri puta u Rimu i u **Lurdu** 2008., o 150. obljetnici ukazanja iz 1858. Biskup je potaknuo i da se posljednji kongres održi u **Međugorju**, kako bi teologija dala svoj doprinos razumijevanju onoga što se ondje događa.
sections.subtitle_en: Mother's songs about Our Lady and fifteen years at the head of the Mariological institute
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about his mother's songs about the Blessed Virgin Mary
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that the bishop taught Mariology, wrote books and songs about Mary, and organized symposiums and the publishing of proceedings. He asks him how important Mary is to him. „She is very dear to me and very important,” the bishop responds. He grew up with his **mother's songs about the Blessed Virgin**, which even today „echo in his ear and heart.” As a child, he loved May and October devotions, and that, he says, „is imprinted on a person's soul.”

He is a member of the **Hrvatski mariološki institut**, and was also its president. He succeeded **Professor Rebić**, who led the institute for 25 years, while he himself led it for 15 years. After him, **Ivan Karlić** was at the head for ten years. Now a transitional period is underway in which the statute is being aligned with the statute of the KBF.

The institute organized **domestic symposiums** that explored the Mariological heritage of individual dioceses, so one was held in Sisak, and others in Dubrovnik, Split, and the Đakovo-Osijek Archdiocese. The members also notably participated in **international congresses**: three times in Rome and in **Lourdes** in 2008, on the 150th anniversary of the apparitions from 1858. The bishop also encouraged the last congress to be held in **Međugorje**, so that theology could make its contribution to understanding what is happening there.

sections.subtitle: Hrvati kao marijanski narod i kajkavska baština o Mariji
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o kajkavskim propovjednicima i svom doktoratu o Franji Ksaveru Pejačeviću
sections.content:
Biskup Košić smatra da su mariologija i marijanska pobožnost jako važne za hrvatski narod. Navodi tezu jednog teologa da su narodi koji su mnogo propatili posebno marijanski, a kao primjere taj je teolog istaknuo poljski, meksički i hrvatski narod. Biskup nije siguran je li to rekao **Suenens** ili netko drugi, ali misao je zapisao u svojoj **mariološkoj skripti**, objavljenoj u *Kršćanskoj sadašnjosti*. Želio bi je ažurirati i izdati kao knjižicu, „ali nema vremena”, a sugovornik mu u tome dovršava misao.

Posebno je volio staru **kajkavsku mariološku baštinu** propovjednika iz 17. i 18. stoljeća. Kajkavski je tada bio književni jezik Hrvatske, *reliquiae reliquiarum olim*, i bio je vrlo razvijen. Kao primjer navodi **Belostenčev** latinsko-kajkavski rječnik. U toj baštini ima mnogo pobožnosti, ali i dogmatske dubine, ovisno o autoru i vremenu.

Za doktorat je proučavao **Franju Ksavera Pejačevića** iz 18. stoljeća. U njegovim dogmatskim radovima na latinskom traktati o Mariji nalaze se uz kristologiju i obuhvaćaju četiri marijanske dogme. Biskup ističe da Hrvatima to „nije samo forma ili ukras”.
sections.subtitle_en: Croats as a Marian people and the Kajkavian heritage about Mary
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about Kajkavian preachers and his doctorate on Franjo Ksaver Pejačević
sections.content_en:
Bishop Košić considers Mariology and Marian devotion to be very important for the Croatian people. He cites a theologian's thesis that peoples who have suffered a great deal are especially Marian, and as examples that theologian highlighted the Polish, Mexican, and Croatian peoples. The bishop is not sure whether **Suenens** or someone else said that, but he wrote down the thought in his **Mariological script**, published in *Kršćanska sadašnjost*. He would like to update it and publish it as a booklet, "but there is no time", and his interlocutor finishes the thought for him.

He especially loved the old **Kajkavian Mariological heritage** of preachers from the 17th and 18th centuries. Kajkavian was then the literary language of Croatia, *reliquiae reliquiarum olim*, and was very developed. As an example he cites **Belostenec's** Latin-Kajkavian dictionary. In that heritage there is much devotion, but also dogmatic depth, depending on the author and the time.

For his doctorate he studied **Franjo Ksaver Pejačević** from the 18th century. In his dogmatic works in Latin, treatises on Mary are located alongside Christology and encompass four Marian dogmas. The bishop emphasizes that for Croats this is "not just form or ornament".

sections.subtitle: „Pjevajte, Kraljice Hrvata”: marijanski papa i hrvatski identitet
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup prepričava kako je papa Ivan Pavao II. hrvatske biskupe poticao da pjevaju Kraljici Hrvata
sections.content:
Kad Hrvati Mariju nazivaju **Kraljicom Hrvata**, zagovornicom i najvjernijom majkom, to je, ističe biskup, nešto „duboko sraslo s našim narodom, poviješću i identitetom”. Vjeruje da ta veza narod čuva i vodi ga da bude vjeran Kristu, kao što je to bila i Marija.

Prisjeća se kako je **sveti papa Ivan Pavao II.** volio tu pjesmu. Tijekom posjeta Hrvatskoj 1994. u Splitu je s mladima pjevao „Zdravo Djevo, kraljice Hrvata”. Kad su mu hrvatski biskupi kasnije došli u pohod *ad limina*, rekao im je: „**Pjevajte, Kraljice Hrvata, o Majko mila**”, jer je zapamtio riječi i htio je pjevati s njima.

Biskup ga naziva **duboko marijanskim papom** i podsjeća da je o toj temi održao predavanje, objavljeno u zborniku izdanom u papinu čast. Zaključuje uvjerenjem da marijanska pobožnost može pomoći hrvatskom narodu da sačuva svoj identitet i „ide dalje u budućnost pravim putem”.
sections.subtitle_en: „Sing, Queen of the Croats”: a Marian pope and Croatian identity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop recounts how Pope John Paul II encouraged Croatian bishops to sing to the Queen of the Croats
sections.content_en:
When Croats call Mary the **Queen of the Croats**, advocate and most faithful mother, that is, the bishop emphasizes, something „deeply grown together with our people, history, and identity”. He believes that this bond protects the people and leads them to be faithful to Christ, just as Mary was.

He recalls how **Saint Pope John Paul II** loved that song. During his visit to Croatia in 1994 in Split, he sang „Hail Virgin, Queen of the Croats” with the youth. When the Croatian bishops later came to him for an *ad limina* visit, he told them: „**Sing, Queen of the Croats, O dear Mother**”, because he remembered the words and wanted to sing with them.

The bishop calls him a **deeply Marian pope** and reminds that he gave a lecture on that topic, published in a collection of papers issued in the Pope's honor. He concludes with the conviction that Marian devotion can help the Croatian people preserve their identity and „go forward into the future on the right path”.
