sections.subtitle: Biskup koji je odlučio sam provjeriti: susret s moliteljima na trgu
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Vlado Košić objašnjava zašto se nije oslanjao na medijske napise, nego je sam došao na javnu molitvu krunice
sections.content:
Razgovor o ljubavi prema Gospi voditelj podcasta **Redefinicija** povezuje s konkretnim iskustvom. Podsjeća da je sisački biskup **mons. Vlado Košić** nekoliko puta sudjelovao na javnoj molitvi krunice. Prvi put to je bilo u **srpnju 2023. u Zagrebu**, a drugi put u **Sisku, u siječnju ove godine**. Voditelj otvoreno priznaje da se o moliteljima pisalo svašta i da mnogi u javnosti nisu uspjeli trezveno i objektivno prosuditi o čemu je riječ. Zato ga zanima kako je biskup doživio to prvo iskustvo na trgu i kako je o njemu kasnije razmišljao.

Odgovor mons. Košića jednostavan je i izravan. Želio je *vidjeti svojim očima*. Kako kaže, nije **nasjeo pričama, napisima ni kritikama**, nego se htio sam uvjeriti. Otišao je i bilo mu je drago što je sudjelovao jer, prema vlastitim riječima, *tu nije vidio nikakvih problema*. To je i javno govorio. Posebno ističe da je zadovoljan što se na tim okupljanjima ne događa ništa protivno Crkvi ni kršćanskoj vjeri.

Biskup otkriva da je osim u Zagrebu i Sisku jednom molio i u **Popovači**. Najavljuje i novi dolazak: molitelji su ga pozvali da u Sisku **blagoslovi njihovu novu zastavu**, pa planira doći na sljedeću molitvu, prve subote u lipnju.
sections.subtitle_en: The bishop who decided to check for himself: an encounter with the prayer warriors on the square
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Vlado Košić explains why he did not rely on media reports, but came in person to the public Rosary prayer
sections.content_en:
The host of the podcast **Redefinicija** connects the conversation about love for Our Lady with a concrete experience. He recalls that the bishop of Sisak, **Msgr. Vlado Košić**, participated several times in the public Rosary prayer. The first time was in **July 2023 in Zagreb**, and the second time in **Sisak, in January of this year**. The host openly admits that all sorts of things were written about the prayer warriors and that many in the public failed to judge soberly and objectively what it was about. Therefore, he is interested in how the bishop experienced that first encounter on the square and how he reflected on it later.

Msgr. Košić's answer is simple and direct. He wanted to *see with his own eyes*. As he says, he did not **fall for stories, articles, or criticisms**, but wanted to convince himself. He went, and he was glad to have participated because, according to his own words, *he saw no problems there*. He also stated this publicly. He particularly emphasizes that he is pleased that nothing contrary to the Church or the Christian faith happens at those gatherings.

The bishop reveals that, besides Zagreb and Sisak, he also prayed once in **Popovača**. He also announces a new arrival: the prayer warriors invited him to **bless their new flag** in Sisak, so he plans to come to the next prayer, on the first Saturday in June.

sections.subtitle: „Nešto proročko“: krunica kao ruka spasa za svijet koji srlja u propast
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić govori da je javna molitva krunice proročki znak vremena
sections.content:
Najsnažniju misao ovog dijela razgovora mons. Košić izgovara kada promišlja širi smisao pokreta. Kada o tome *malo više razmisli*, kaže, čini mu se da je riječ o **znaku vremena**. Sam priznaje da ne zna točno kakav je to znak, ali u toj pojavi vidi *nešto proročko*. Naglašava da pokret nije nastao samo u Hrvatskoj. Prije toga postojao je u **Poljskoj**, a i drugdje su se okupljali muževi koji su željeli svjedočiti svoju vjeru upravo moleći krunicu.

Biskup to tumači kao znak da **odgovorni katolički muževi vide kako svijet srlja u propast** i da u Mariji vide, kako kaže tražeći pravu riječ, *ruku spasa*. Prema njegovim riječima, molitelji žele da Gospa svojim zagovorom:

- **utvrdi katoličke muževe**,
- **ojača katoličke obitelji**, kako bi one doista bile ono što bi trebale biti,
- pomogne vjernicima da se **odupru navalama i zamkama** koje se danas postavljaju pred njih.

Svoje promišljanje zaključuje ozbiljnom dijagnozom suvremenog trenutka: kako i sami gledatelji vide, *sve je više zla u koje tone čitav svijet*. Javnu molitvu krunice zato ne doživljava kao folklor ni kao demonstraciju, nego kao duhovni odgovor na krizu vremena.
sections.subtitle_en: "Something prophetic": the Rosary as a saving hand for a world hurtling toward ruin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić says that the public prayer of the Rosary is a prophetic sign of the times
sections.content_en:
Monsignor Košić utters the strongest thought of this part of the conversation when reflecting on the broader meaning of the movement. When he *thinks a little more* about it, he says, it seems to him that it is a **sign of the times**. He admits himself that he does not know exactly what kind of sign it is, but in this phenomenon he sees *something prophetic*. He emphasizes that the movement did not originate only in Croatia. Before that, it existed in **Poland**, and elsewhere men were also gathering who wanted to witness to their faith precisely by praying the Rosary.

The Bishop interprets this as a sign that **responsible Catholic men see how the world is hurtling toward ruin** and that in Mary they see, as he says searching for the right word, *a saving hand*. According to his words, the men praying desire that Our Lady, through her intercession:

- **strengthen Catholic men**,
- **strengthen Catholic families**, so that they truly are what they should be,
- help the faithful to **resist the assaults and snares** that are placed before them today.

He concludes his reflection with a serious diagnosis of the contemporary moment: as the viewers themselves see, *there is more and more evil into which the whole world is sinking*. Therefore, he does not perceive the public prayer of the Rosary as folklore nor as a demonstration, but as a spiritual response to the crisis of the times.

sections.subtitle: Promrzli prsti i utihnuli vjetar: sisačko svjedočanstvo i skromnost biskupa
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić skromno odbacuje pripisivanje nadnaravnih moći svom blagoslovu
sections.content:
Voditelj ističe da je moliteljima mnogo značilo kada je biskup došao, **kleknuo s njima i molio**. Prema voditeljevim riječima, to je bilo lijepo svjedočanstvo. Zatim prenosi dirljivu priču koju su ispričala „braća iz Siska“. Na siječanjskoj molitvi u Sisku bilo je **jako hladno**, puhao je snažan vjetar i moliteljima su se smrzavale ruke. Upravo tada stigao je biskup i podijelio blagoslov. Čim je počela molitva, osjetili su kako se **promrzlim prstima vraća toplina** i kako im *krv ponovno kola venama*. Kako tvrde, vrijeme se smirilo, a vjetar je utihnuo. Molitelji su to povezali s biskupovim blagoslovom i autoritetom. Voditelj ga zato pita je li svjestan *moći blagoslova* koju ima kao biskup.

Sugovornik napominje da to iskustvo može biti i subjektivno, ali da je riječ o lijepom svjedočanstvu. Mons. Košić odgovara s vidljivom suzdržanošću. Priču je i sam čuo, ali kaže da se *ne bi tako izjasnio*. **„Nemam ja nikakve nadzemaljske moći“**, naglašava. Sebe vidi kao **slugu Crkve i Kristova**.

Ipak, vrijednost blagoslova ne umanjuje. Podsjeća da mu i sama riječ kaže da *blago djeluje na ljude*. Zazivati Božje ime i zaštitu Blažene Djevice Marije za ljude i za cijeli svijet sigurno je, kako kaže, *korisno i djelotvorno*. Priču zaključuje slikovito: blagoslov može pomoći da se *otope neki ledovi i snjegovi*, ali to radije tumači kao **duhovnu nego kao fizičku stvarnost**.
sections.subtitle_en: Frozen fingers and silenced wind: a testimony from Sisak and the bishop's modesty
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić modestly rejects attributing supernatural powers to his blessing
sections.content_en:
The host points out that it meant a lot to the prayer participants when the bishop arrived, **knelt with them and prayed**. According to the host's words, it was a beautiful testimony. Then he shares a touching story told by the "brothers from Sisak". At the January prayer in Sisak it was **very cold**, a strong wind was blowing and the prayer participants' hands were freezing. Right then the bishop arrived and imparted a blessing. As soon as the prayer began, they felt **warmth returning to their frozen fingers** and *blood circulating in their veins again*. As they claim, the weather calmed down, and the wind fell silent. The prayer participants connected this with the bishop's blessing and authority. The host therefore asks him whether he is aware of the *power of blessing* that he has as a bishop.

The interlocutor notes that this experience may also be subjective, but that it is a beautiful testimony. Msgr. Košić responds with visible restraint. He heard the story himself, but says that he *would not express himself that way*. **"I do not have any supernatural powers"**, he emphasizes. He sees himself as a **servant of the Church and of Christ**.

Nevertheless, he does not diminish the value of a blessing. He recalls that the very word itself says that it *acts gently on people*. Calling upon God's name and the protection of the Blessed Virgin Mary for people and for the whole world is certainly, as he says, *beneficial and effective*. He concludes the story vividly: a blessing can help *melt some ice and snow*, but he prefers to interpret this as a **spiritual rather than a physical reality**.

sections.subtitle: Hod za život nije politika, nego kršćanska i moralna obveza
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić objašnjava da podrškom Hodu za život ne podupire nijednu političku stranku
sections.content:
Osim pokreta javne molitve krunice, voditelj ističe da biskup daje potporu i **pokretu za život**. Sudjelovao je i na prvom sisačkom **Hodu za život**. Mons. Košić pojašnjava da je na Hodu sudjelovao više puta. Nije siguran je li bio baš na svakom, ali koliko zna, ove bi godine trebalo biti sedmo ili osmo izdanje. Dolazi i ovaj put: Hod za život kroz Sisak ponovno se održava **20. lipnja**.

Odlučno odbacuje tvrdnje da je riječ o političkoj manifestaciji. Kako kaže, neki je *žele tako prikazati*. Neki su čak i njega ukorili da se time ne bavi jer je to navodno politika u koju se *biskup ne treba pačati*. Njegov odgovor kritičarima jasan je: **ne čini to iz političkih razloga i ne podupire nijednu političku stranku**. Podupire svijest da su vjernici dužni **braniti život od začeća do prirodne smrti**.

To naziva *kršćanskom i moralnom obvezom*. U toj se ulozi, objašnjava, pojavljuje kao vjernik, ali i kao autoritet, na što se nadovezuje na voditeljevo ranije pitanje. Svoju poziciju sažima rečenicom koja ne ostavlja mjesta dvojbi: ako je on onaj koji vodi Crkvu, onda *ne može, neće i ne smije biti protiv života*.
sections.subtitle_en: The Walk for Life is not politics, but a Christian and moral obligation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Košić explains that by supporting the Walk for Life, he does not support any political party
sections.content_en:
In addition to the public Rosary prayer movement, the host points out that the bishop also gives support to the **movement for life**. He also participated in the first Sisak **Walk for Life**. Msgr. Košić clarifies that he has participated in the Walk multiple times. He is not sure if he was at every single one, but as far as he knows, this year should be the seventh or eighth edition. He is coming this time as well: the Walk for Life through Sisak is being held again on **June 20**.

He firmly rejects claims that it is a political manifestation. As he says, some *want to portray it that way*. Some even rebuked him not to deal with it because it is allegedly politics in which *a bishop should not meddle*. His response to critics is clear: **he does not do this for political reasons and does not support any political party**. He supports the awareness that believers are obliged to **defend life from conception to natural death**.

He calls this a *Christian and moral obligation*. In that role, he explains, he appears as a believer, but also as an authority, which connects to the host's earlier question. He summarizes his position with a sentence that leaves no room for doubt: if he is the one who leads the Church, then *he cannot, will not, and must not be against life*.

sections.subtitle: Ponoćka pred kamerama: propovijed za nerođene
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup prepričava božićnu propovijed o zaštiti nerođenog života prenošenu na televiziji
sections.content:
Kao primjer svoje dosljednosti mons. Košić prisjeća se jedne **ponoćke u sisačkoj katedrali**, još prije potresa. Misu je tada snimala televizija. Propovijed je pripremio svjesno, znajući da je te godine trebao biti donesen novi zakon. Prema njegovim riječima, jedan sud (ne sjeća se je li bio Ustavni ili Vrhovni) naložio je da se sljedeće godine *ispravi zakon iz Jugoslavije* i donese novi propis o **zaštiti čovjekova života od začeća**. To se, kako napominje, nije dogodilo.

U propovijedi se pozvao na riječi jedne dobitnice nagrade za mir: **ne može biti mira u svijetu ako se ne poštuje život**. Biskup razvija tu logiku. Ako se smije ubiti nerođeno dijete, koje se ne može braniti, *što će onda biti s onima koji se mogu braniti?* Tada se, upozorava, *može sve ubijati*. Upravo se to, smatra, i događa jer se život zapravo ne štiti.

I ta je propovijed izazvala kritike. Neki su mu zamjerili što je *iskoristio priliku* kada je bila prisutna televizija. Biskup ne odstupa: govorio je baš zato da njegove riječi *dopru do ušiju barem nekih* koji trebaju odgovorno postupati s ljudskim životom, s nerođenim čovjekom i djetetom. Htio je javno pokazati da se **katolici zalažu za život**. „I tu nemam ja dileme“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Midnight Mass in Front of the Cameras: A Homily for the Unborn
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop recounts a Christmas homily on the protection of unborn life broadcast on television
sections.content_en:
As an example of his consistency, Msgr. Košić recalls a **Midnight Mass in the Sisak cathedral**, even before the earthquake. Mass was being filmed by television at the time. He prepared the homily deliberately, knowing that a new law was supposed to be passed that year. According to his words, a court (he does not remember whether it was the Constitutional or the Supreme Court) ordered that the following year the *law from Yugoslavia be corrected* and a new regulation be passed on the **protection of human life from conception**. That, as he notes, did not happen.

In the homily, he referred to the words of a peace prize winner: **there can be no peace in the world if life is not respected**. The bishop develops this logic. If it is permissible to kill an unborn child, who cannot defend itself, *what then will happen to those who can defend themselves?* Then, he warns, *everything can be killed*. That, he believes, is precisely what is happening because life is actually not protected.

And that homily provoked criticism. Some reproached him for having *used the opportunity* when television was present. The bishop does not back down: he spoke precisely so that his words would *reach the ears of at least some* who need to act responsibly with human life, with the unborn human being and child. He wanted to show publicly that **Catholics stand up for life**. “And there I have no dilemma,” he concludes.

sections.subtitle: „Psi laju, karavana prolazi“: medijski napadi i mjesto laika u Crkvi
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić odgovara na pitanje o medijskim napadima i ističe da je Crkva prije svega zajednica vjernika laika
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da je biskup zbog otvorenosti prema pokretima koje su prije svega pokrenuli laici često na **meti medija**. Pita ga kako te napade proživljava i kako se nosi sa svim tim naslovima.

Mons. Košić odgovor počinje eklesiološkom lekcijom, temom koju je i sam predavao. **Crkva nisu samo biskupi ni svećenici, dapače, većinu Crkve čine vjernici laici.** Zato, kaže, biskupi ne mogu biti oni koji određuju što će se, a što neće pokretati u Crkvi. Njihova je zadaća drugačija: *prepoznati ono što je dobro i to poduprijeti*.

Zatim postavlja retorička pitanja. Kako bi mogao biti protiv inicijative koja je u biti dobra i ima dobar cilj? *Kako bi biskup mogao biti protiv krunice, protiv molitve?* Ili reći da su oni koji se bore za zaštitu života na krivom putu? Biskup, smatra, treba iznositi moralni stav Katoličke crkve, a svatko može sam pogledati što piše u **Katekizmu Katoličke crkve**. Takve prigovore ne može ni dovesti u pitanje: *samo odmahne rukom*.

Napade ne poriče: zna da postoje i da ga ne štede. Ali komentira ih poslovicom **„psi laju, karavana prolazi“**. Smatra da su prolazni, *neka moda*, i da neki napadima traže priliku da se o njima govori, svejedno dobro ili loše. Današnji medijski svijet, upozorava, *pun je zamki*. Vjernici ne trebaju i ne žele medijsku slavu. Pozivajući se na **svetog Pavla**, zaključuje da se dobro čini bez obzira na to hoće li ljudi pljeskati ili gađati kamenjem, bilo to zgodno ili nezgodno, jer treba **braniti istinu i činiti dobro**. To, kaže, smatra svojom dužnošću.
sections.subtitle_en: “The dogs bark, the caravan passes”: media attacks and the place of the laity in the Church
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Košić answers a question about media attacks and emphasizes that the Church is above all a community of lay faithful
sections.content_en:
The host notes that the bishop, because of his openness to movements initiated primarily by the laity, is often a **media target**. He asks him how he experiences those attacks and how he deals with all those headlines.

Msgr. Košić begins his answer with an ecclesiological lesson, a topic he himself used to teach. **The Church is not only bishops or priests; indeed, the majority of the Church consists of the lay faithful.** Therefore, he says, bishops cannot be the ones who determine what will and what will not be initiated in the Church. Their task is different: *to recognize what is good and support it*.

Then he asks rhetorical questions. How could he be against an initiative that is essentially good and has a good goal? *How could a bishop be against the Rosary, against prayer?* Or say that those who fight for the protection of life are on the wrong path? A bishop, he believes, should present the moral stance of the Catholic Church, and anyone can look for themselves at what is written in the **Catechism of the Catholic Church**. Such objections he cannot even call into question: *he simply waves his hand*.

He does not deny the attacks: he knows they exist and that they do not spare him. But he comments on them with the proverb **“the dogs bark, the caravan passes”**. He considers them fleeting, *a sort of fashion*, and that some seek an opportunity through attacks to be talked about, whether good or bad. Today's media world, he warns, *is full of traps*. The faithful do not need and do not want media fame. Referring to **Saint Paul**, he concludes that good is done regardless of whether people will applaud or throw stones, whether convenient or inconvenient, because one must **defend the truth and do good**. That, he says, he considers his duty.

sections.subtitle: Stepinac kao zaštitnik: spoj vjere i domoljublja
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić govori o blaženom Alojziju Stepincu kao svom zaštitniku i uzoru
sections.content:
Na pitanje odakle crpi snagu i tko mu je sveti zaštitnik, mons. Košić odgovara epizodom iz razgovora s **apostolskim nuncijem, nadbiskupom Linguom**. Nuncij ga je ispitivao o nekim stvarima jer su ga, kako kaže, *neki napadali i tužili*. Biskup mu je tada odgovorio: **„Ja slijedim blaženog Alojzija Stepinca.“**

Objašnjava i zašto. Stepinac je blaženik Katoličke crkve koji je **branio istinu**. Govorio je **protiv komunizma**, **protiv nacizma**, protiv svakog zločina i protiv zatiranja ljudskih prava. Ako je to bilo ispravno za blaženika, zaključuje biskup, *valjda i on ima pravo* jednako zastupati ono što je za dobro čovjeka i naroda.

Posebno ističe da je Stepinac bio **osobiti ljubitelj svoga naroda** i da je **spajao vjeru i domoljublje**. Mons. Košić smatra da je i sam na neki način upio taj spoj, ponajviše kroz vlastita ratna iskustva.
sections.subtitle_en: Stepinac as patron: the union of faith and patriotism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić speaks about Blessed Alojzije Stepinac as his patron and role model
sections.content_en:
To the question of where he draws strength from and who his patron saint is, Msgr. Košić responds with an episode from a conversation with the **apostolic nuncio, Archbishop Lingua**. The nuncio questioned him about certain matters because, as he says, *some were attacking and accusing him*. The bishop then answered him: **"I follow Blessed Alojzije Stepinac."**

He also explains why. Stepinac is a blessed of the Catholic Church who **defended the truth**. He spoke **against communism**, **against Nazism**, against every crime and against the suppression of human rights. If that was right for the blessed, the bishop concludes, *surely he too has the right* to equally advocate for what is for the good of man and the nation.

He particularly emphasizes that Stepinac was a **particular lover of his people** and that he **united faith and patriotism**. Msgr. Košić considers that he himself in some way absorbed that union, mostly through his own wartime experiences.

sections.subtitle: David protiv Golijata: pravedan rat i stotine krunica za branitelje
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić govori o Domovinskom ratu kao pravednom obrambenom ratu i o krunicama koje je dijelio braniteljima
sections.content:
Nadovezujući se na ratna iskustva, biskup odlučno odbacuje relativizaciju rata. Odbija sliku prema kojoj su *jedni i drugi zli ili dobri, svi jednaki* i *tuku se bez veze, ne zna se zašto*. „Pa nije tako“, kaže. S jedne strane bila je **agresija i napad na nevine ljude**, a s druge strane **obrana koja je imala pravednu oznaku**. Bio je to, naglašava, **pravedan, obrambeni rat** i strane ne može izjednačiti *u svojoj savjesti*.

Podsjeća na riječi **kardinala Kuharića** da je to bilo *čudo Božje*. Poseže za biblijskom slikom: ako se David odupro Golijatu i nadvladao ga, Bog je bio s njim. Prema tome je, zaključuje, *Bog bio i s Hrvatima* kada su se u nemogućim okolnostima izborili za opstanak. Pritom ističe da nije bila riječ o tome tko će koga nadjačati, nego o pitanju **biti ili ne biti**.

Zato je, kaže, krunica tada bila iznimno važna. Biskup je **podijelio stotine krunica hrvatskim braniteljima**. Ona je označavala Božju zaštitu i zaštitu Blažene Djevice Marije, ali je donosila i obvezu. Tko nosi krunicu oko vrata, treba biti vjeran svojoj katoličkoj vjeri, zaštiti Majke Božje i **križu Kristovu** koji visi na kraju krunice. To je, smatra, bila pouka i za neprijatelje i za branitelje. Prisjeća se i tvrdnje da *takve vojske nikad nije bilo* koja bi na odori nosila krunicu: „To su imali Hrvati. I to nas obvezuje.“
sections.subtitle_en: David versus Goliath: A Just War and Hundreds of Rosaries for Defenders
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mons. Košić speaks about the Homeland War as a just defensive war and about the rosaries he distributed to defenders
sections.content_en:
Drawing upon wartime experiences, the bishop decisively rejects the relativization of war. He rejects the depiction according to which *both sides are evil or good, everyone is equal* and *they are fighting pointlessly, no one knows why*. “Well, that is not so,” he says. On one side there was **aggression and an attack on innocent people**, and on the other side **a defense that bore the mark of justice**. It was, he emphasizes, **a just, defensive war** and he cannot equate the sides *in his conscience*.

He recalls the words of **Cardinal Kuharić** that it was *a miracle of God*. He reaches for a biblical image: if David resisted Goliath and overcame him, God was with him. Accordingly, he concludes, *God was also with the Croats* when they fought for survival under impossible circumstances. At the same time, he points out that it was not a matter of who would overpower whom, but a question of **to be or not to be**.

That is why, he says, the Rosary was exceptionally important at that time. The bishop **distributed hundreds of rosaries to Croatian defenders**. It signified God's protection and the protection of the Blessed Virgin Mary, but it also brought an obligation. Whoever wears a rosary around their neck must be faithful to their Catholic faith, to the protection of the Mother of God, and to the **cross of Christ** that hangs at the end of the rosary. That, he believes, was a lesson both for enemies and for defenders. He also recalls the claim that *there had never been such an army* that would wear a rosary on their uniform: “The Croats had that. And that obligates us.”

sections.subtitle: Hoće li papa Lav XIV. proglasiti Stepinca svetim?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita biskupa o susretima s papama i o mogućoj kanonizaciji Stepinca
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da se mons. Košić tijekom života susreo s nizom papa: od **Ivana Pavla II.**, preko **Benedikta** i **Franje**, do **pape Lava**. Pita ga kakvo je njegovo mišljenje o novom papi i vjeruje li da će upravo on proglasiti svetim blaženog Alojzija Stepinca.

Biskup odgovara bez oklijevanja: **vjeruje da hoće**. Dodaje da ni papa Franjo nije imao razloga da ga ne proglasi. Ipak, Franjo je, kako kaže, smatrao da je potrebno *zastati* i vidjeti koliko se može ići ususret **istočnim kršćanima**. Oni, prema biskupovim riječima, imaju neke svoje razloge, ali *imaju i mitove*.
sections.subtitle_en: Will Pope Leo XIV declare Stepinac a saint?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the bishop about meetings with popes and about the possible canonization of Stepinac
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that Msgr. Košić has met with a series of popes during his lifetime: from **John Paul II**, through **Benedict** and **Francis**, to **Pope Leo**. He asks him what his opinion is of the new pope and whether he believes that it will be he who declares Blessed Alojzije Stepinac a saint.

The bishop responds without hesitation: **he believes he will**. He adds that Pope Francis did not have a reason not to declare him one either. Nevertheless, Francis, as he says, considered that it was necessary to *pause* and see how far one could accommodate **Eastern Christians**. They, according to the bishop's words, have some reasons of their own, but *they also have myths*.

sections.subtitle: Zastoj iz 2014.: mitovi, mješovita komisija i istina koja se ne smije žrtvovati
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić naglašava da se istina o Stepincu ne smije žrtvovati
sections.content:
Mons. Košić detaljno opisuje kako je došlo do zastoja kanonizacije. Prema njegovim riječima, **sastanci mješovite komisije pokazali su da argumenata protiv Stepinca nema**. Ljudi ipak, kaže, *žive u svojim umišljajima i strahovima*, a papa Franjo želio je da se to nekako ukloni pa je proces zaustavio.

Prisjeća se kronologije iz **2014. godine**. **Kardinal Amato** objavio je da je **Kongregacija za svece** završila sav posao i da preostaje samo da papa Stepinca proglasi svetim. To je učinio **10. veljače**, na blagdan blaženog Alojzija Stepinca, u **crkvi svetog Jeronima u Rimu**. Biskup smatra da se kardinal tada *malo zaletio* jer to nije bilo na njemu da kaže. Ipak, bio je jako radostan i želio je to podijeliti s Hrvatima, koje je volio. Već u travnju stigla je, međutim, **molba srpskog patrijarha** i proces je zaustavljen kako bi se vidjelo može li se pravoslavnoj strani nešto olakšati.

Biskup ne poriče da je papin napor donio i **mnogo dobra Crkvi u Hrvatskoj**. U tom su vremenu mnogi bolje upoznali lik blaženog Alojzija, kojega ranije nisu poznavali. Ali odlučno ponavlja: **„Istina se ne smije žrtvovati.“** Istina je, kaže, već dokazana, a *potvrdio ju je i dragi Bog* čudom po Stepinčevu zagovoru. Zato nema razloga da se proces ne završi, osim što će to *neke ljude ili neki narod boljeti*. Pritom se pita tko pita Katoličku crkvu kakve se svece proglašava u drugim crkvama.

Svoju obranu potkrepljuje činjenicama o Stepinčevu djelovanju. Postoje, kaže, pravi argumenti koji govore u prilog blaženiku: **činio je dobro i srpskom i židovskom narodu**, kao i mnogim nevjernicima koje je za vrijeme rata spašavao od progona. Biskupu je to jedna od Stepinčevih najvećih odlika. Bio je *čovjek velike širine duha* koji, kada je trebalo pomoći, *nije gledao tko je tko*, jer je bio **Božji čovjek**. Oni koji su u krivu, zaključuje, trebaju prihvatiti da nema nijednog argumenta i prihvatiti istinu.
sections.subtitle_en: The 2014 stall: myths, the mixed commission, and the truth that must not be sacrificed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mons. Košić emphasizes that the truth about Stepinac must not be sacrificed
sections.content_en:
Mons. Košić describes in detail how the stall in the canonization came about. According to his words, **the meetings of the mixed commission showed that there are no arguments against Stepinac**. People nevertheless, he says, *live in their delusions and fears*, and Pope Francis wanted this to somehow be removed, so he stopped the process.

He recalls the chronology from the **year 2014**. **Cardinal Amato** announced that the **Congregation for the Causes of Saints** had finished all the work and that it only remained for the Pope to declare Stepinac a saint. He did this on **February 10**, on the feast day of Blessed Alojzije Stepinac, in the **Church of Saint Jerome in Rome**. The bishop considers that the cardinal *got a little ahead of himself* then because it was not up to him to say that. Still, he was very joyful and wanted to share that with the Croats, whom he loved. Already in April, however, the **request of the Serbian Patriarch** arrived, and the process was stopped in order to see whether something could be eased for the Orthodox side.

The bishop does not deny that the Pope's effort also brought **much good to the Church in Croatia**. During that time, many came to know better the figure of Blessed Alojzije, whom they did not know earlier. But he resolutely repeats: **"The truth must not be sacrificed."** The truth has, he says, already been proven, and *dear God also confirmed it* with a miracle through Stepinac's intercession. Therefore, there is no reason for the process not to be completed, except that it will *hurt some people or a certain nation*. At the same time, he wonders who asks the Catholic Church what kind of saints are declared in other churches.

He supports his defense with facts about Stepinac's actions. There are, he says, real arguments that speak in favor of the blessed: **he did good to both the Serbian and the Jewish people**, as well as to many unbelievers whom he saved from persecution during the war. To the bishop, that is one of Stepinac's greatest qualities. He was a *man of great breadth of spirit* who, when help was needed, *did not look at who was who*, because he was a **man of God**. Those who are in the wrong, he concludes, should accept that there is not a single argument and accept the truth.
entities_en: Congregation for the Causes of Saints

sections.subtitle: Spomenik u Sisku i kozaračka djeca: „Siščani trebaju biti ponosni“
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić govori o spašavanju kozaračke djece i spomeniku Stepincu s dvoje djece u Sisku
sections.content:
Mons. Košić prisjeća se izjave koja je, priznaje, mogla zvučati *malo provokativno*. Rekao je da bi ekumenski dijalog sa **Srpskom pravoslavnom crkvom** trebalo nastaviti *ako i kada podignu spomenik blaženom Alojziju Stepincu u Beogradu*. Za usporedbu navodi Sisak, gdje je održan simpozij i gdje je **2018. podignut spomenik Stepincu**, prikazanom zajedno s **dvoje djece**.

Simbolika nije slučajna. Stepinac je, objašnjava biskup, **spašavao djecu, među njima i kozaračku**. Pitanje „tko ih je ubijao“ biskup odbacuje tvrdnjom da ih *nitko nije ubijao*. Djeca su, prema njegovim riječima, stizala gladna, bolesna i već umiruća, i trebalo ih je zbrinuti. Stepinac je organizirao pomoć u kojoj su sudjelovali **katolički svećenici, časne sestre i obitelji**. Prema biskupovim riječima, uključili su se i liječnici, sestre iz državnih i crkvenih udruga te vjernici koji su djecu udomljavali.

Brojke koje navodi pokazuju razmjere te akcije:

- u grad je stiglo **otprilike 6000 djece**, što bi bio problem i za veliki Zagreb, a kamoli za manji grad u ratu i gladi,
- **oko 5000 ih je preživjelo**,
- nešto više od tisuću, *1100 negdje*, umrlo je, i to, naglašava biskup, **od gladi i bolesti, a ne nasilnom smrću**.

Preživjeli su i danas svjedoci da su ih spasili *dobri ljudi, naši sugrađani*. Zato mons. Košić ponavlja ono što je već više puta rekao: **Siščani trebaju biti ponosni** jer su spasili mnogo kozaračke, srpske ili pravoslavne djece, kako god ih tko nazvao. Tvrdnja da su Hrvati ubijali djecu duboko ga vrijeđa. „Ako već nisi zahvalan, nemoj biti toliko drzak da lažeš. Reci istinu, a ako nećeš, onda šuti“, poručuje, priznajući da je tada bio emotivan.
sections.subtitle_en: The monument in Sisak and the Kozara children: „The people of Sisak should be proud“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić speaks about the rescue of the Kozara children and the monument to Stepinac with two children in Sisak
sections.content_en:
Msgr. Košić recalls a statement that, he admits, could have sounded *a little provocative*. He said that ecumenical dialogue with the **Serbian Orthodox Church** should be continued *if and when they erect a monument to Blessed Alojzije Stepinac in Beograd*. For comparison, he cites Sisak, where a symposium was held and where **in 2018 a monument to Stepinac was erected**, depicting him together with **two children**.

The symbolism is not accidental. Stepinac, the bishop explains, **rescued children, among them also the Kozara children**. The question of „who was killing them“ the bishop dismisses with the claim that *no one was killing them*. The children, according to his words, were arriving hungry, sick, and already dying, and they needed to be taken care of. Stepinac organized aid in which **Catholic priests, nuns, and families** participated. According to the bishop's words, doctors, nurses from state and Church associations, and faithful who fostered the children also got involved.

The figures he cites show the scale of that operation:

- **approximately 6,000 children** arrived in the town, which would have been a problem even for large Zagreb, let alone for a smaller town in war and famine,
- **around 5,000 of them survived**,
- slightly more than a thousand, *somewhere around 1,100*, died, and that, the bishop emphasizes, **from hunger and disease, not a violent death**.

The survivors are witnesses even today that they were saved by *good people, our fellow citizens*. That is why Msgr. Košić repeats what he has already said several times: **The people of Sisak should be proud** because they saved many Kozara, Serbian, or Orthodox children, whatever anyone calls them. The claim that Croats were killing children deeply offends him. „If you are already not grateful, do not be so insolent as to lie. Tell the truth, and if you will not, then keep silent,“ he states, admitting that he was emotional at the time.
keywords_en: pride of the people of Sisak

sections.subtitle: Dijalog da, ali ne pod cijenu istine
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić objašnjava da katolički dijalog mora biti razborit i dostojanstven
sections.content:
Svoje stajalište o dijalogu biskup objašnjava osobnom usporedbom. Kada bi netko o njegovu ocu govorio da je bio ubojica ili nasilnik i pripisivao mu ono što nije činio, rekao bi mu da *prestane govoriti neistine* jer s njim tako ne može razgovarati. Prema njegovu mišljenju, to je **pitanje dostojanstva** i samog sugovornika i razine dijaloga.

Oštro kritizira, kako kaže, prividni dijalog u kojem se *grli i slika pred kamerama, jede, pije i slavi*, dok druga strana *drži nož iza leđa*. „Je li to dijalog koji bi trebao biti katolički dijalog?“, pita.

Njegov odgovor nije odbacivanje dijaloga. Naprotiv, naglašava da su katolici **apsolutno za dijalog** i da treba činiti sve kako bi se **približili istok i zapad**. Katolici se moraju znati suzdržati, biti *i diplomati* te ponegdje popustiti. Ali katolički dijalog mora biti **razborit dijalog**, a jedna granica ostaje nepomična: **istinu ne smijemo žrtvovati**.
sections.subtitle_en: Dialogue yes, but not at the price of truth
sections.screenshot_description_en: Msgr. Košić explains that Catholic dialogue must be prudent and dignified
sections.content_en:
The bishop explains his stance on dialogue with a personal comparison. If someone were to say about his father that he was a murderer or a violent person and attribute to him what he did not do, he would tell him to *stop speaking falsehoods* because he cannot speak with him that way. In his opinion, that is **a matter of dignity** both of the interlocutor himself and of the level of dialogue.

He sharply criticizes, as he says, apparent dialogue in which people *hug and take pictures in front of the cameras, eat, drink, and celebrate*, while the other side *holds a knife behind its back*. “Is that the dialogue that should be Catholic dialogue?”, he asks.

His answer is not a rejection of dialogue. On the contrary, he emphasizes that Catholics are **absolutely for dialogue** and that everything should be done in order to **bring East and West closer**. Catholics must know how to restrain themselves, be *diplomats as well*, and give in somewhere. But Catholic dialogue must be **prudent dialogue**, and one boundary remains immovable: **we must not sacrifice the truth**.

sections.subtitle: Od Župnika do Biskupa na prvoj crti: propovijedi, poezija i razgovor sa svetim Petrom
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pokazuje knjigu Biskup na prvoj crti, a gost objašnjava kako je nastala
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na bogat pisani opus mons. Košića. Uz knjigu **„Župnik na prvoj crti“** izašao je i nastavak **„Biskup na prvoj crti“**, koji voditelj pokazuje u studiju. Biskup je napisao i **zbirku poezije**, a ima i talent za pjevanje. Voditelja zanima postoji li još koji talent za koji javnost ne zna.

Biskup najprije pojašnjava nastanak druge knjige. „Biskupa na prvoj crti“ predložili su mu suradnici nakon izlaska „Župnika na prvoj crti“. Knjiga ne sadrži novo pisanje, nego **propovijedi i govore koje je već održao**. Naslov, kaže, ne znači da se predstavlja kao *biskup na prvoj crti*. Odnosi se na biskupiju i područje, osobito ono **između Une i Kupe**, koje je u svim ratovima bilo područje velikih osvajanja i razaranja te velike patnje hrvatskoga katoličkog puka. U knjizi su, među ostalim, govori iz **Bleiburga** i iz **Ludbrega 2016.** te tumačenja **socijalnog nauka Crkve** o tome kako bi se katolici trebali odnositi prema politici. Opet naglašava da *nije favorizirao ni propagirao nijednu stranku*, kako su to neki htjeli prikazati, jer se može pročitati što je zapravo rekao.

Zbirku poezije, otkriva, *pabirčio je još od studentskih dana*. Kako ne bi bile samo pjesme, dodao je i nekoliko **crtica**. U jednoj od njih, nastaloj tijekom pohoda **ad limina**, zamislio je razgovor sa **svetim Petrom**: kako je Petar došao u **Rim**, središte carstva, a Isus nije. Ta ga je misao zanimala, pa ju je *malo problematizirao*. U zbirku je uvrstio i tridesetak **molitava** kojima je uglavnom završavao svoje propovijedi.
sections.subtitle_en: From Parish Priest to Bishop on the Front Line: Sermons, Poetry, and a Conversation with Saint Peter
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host shows the book Bishop on the Front Line, and the guest explains how it came to be
sections.content_en:
The host recalls the rich written opus of Msgr. Košić. Along with the book **“Parish Priest on the Front Line”**, the sequel **“Bishop on the Front Line”** has also been published, which the host shows in the studio. The bishop has also written a **poetry collection**, and he also has a talent for singing. The host is interested in whether there is any other talent that the public does not know about.

The bishop first clarifies the origin of the second book. “Bishop on the Front Line” was suggested to him by collaborators after the release of “Parish Priest on the Front Line”. The book does not contain new writing, but **sermons and speeches he had already delivered**. The title, he says, does not mean that he presents himself as a *bishop on the front line*. It refers to the diocese and the area, especially the one **between the Una and the Kupa**, which in all wars was an area of great conquests and devastation as well as great suffering of the Croatian Catholic people. In the book are, among others, speeches from **Bleiburg** and from **Ludbreg 2016**, as well as interpretations of the **social teaching of the Church** on how Catholics should relate to politics. He again emphasizes that he *did not favor or propagate any party*, as some wanted to portray it, because one can read what he actually said.

The poetry collection, he reveals, he *had been gleaning ever since his student days*. So that it would not be only poems, he also added several **short sketches**. In one of them, created during the **ad limina** visit, he imagined a conversation with **Saint Peter**: how Peter came to **Rome**, the center of the empire, and Jesus did not. That thought intrigued him, so he *problematized it a little*. In the collection he also included about thirty **prayers** with which he mostly ended his sermons.
keywords_en: Parish Priest on the Front Line

sections.subtitle: Deset godina u komisiji Justitia et Pax
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup govori o iskustvu vođenja komisije HBK Justitia et Pax
sections.content:
Mons. Košić otkriva odakle dolaze njegovi stavovi o društvenim i političkim pitanjima. Do njih je, kaže, došao i zato što je **deset godina bio na čelu komisije HBK Justitia et Pax**.

To razdoblje opisuje s mnogo zahvalnosti. Imao je, kako kaže, **dobru ekipu stručnjaka i doktora znanosti** koji su razumjeli stvari. Mnogo je naučio od njih, a zajedno su se *borili za pravedne stvari*.

To iskustvo, zaključuje, oblikovalo ga je jednako kao i rat te kao područje biskupije u kojem djeluje i za koje je postavljen za pastira.
sections.subtitle_en: Ten years on the Justitia et Pax commission
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop speaks about the experience of leading the HBK Justitia et Pax commission
sections.content_en:
Msgr. Košić reveals where his stances on social and political issues come from. He arrived at them, he says, also because **for ten years he was at the head of the HBK Justitia et Pax commission**.

He describes that period with much gratitude. He had, as he says, **a good team of experts and doctors of science** who understood things. He learned a lot from them, and together they *fought for just causes*.

That experience, he concludes, shaped him just as much as the war and as the territory of the diocese in which he works and for which he was appointed as shepherd.

sections.subtitle: Gitara, utakmice i krunica uz Kupu
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup Košić s osmijehom priča o šetnjama uz Kupu s krunicom u ruci
sections.content:
Na pitanje o talentima biskup spominje **glazbu**. Pjeva sada uglavnom na svetim misama, u liturgiji. Gitaru još ponekad uzme, ali sve rjeđe. Nekad je znao zapjevati u društvu ili u opuštenoj atmosferi, no za to sada, priznaje, nema mnogo vremena.

Volio je i **sport, nogomet i košarku**, ali danas uglavnom samo gleda utakmice. S osmijehom dodaje da *nije ni u dobi* u kojoj bi se mogao aktivno baviti sportom.

Najviše od svega voli **šetnje**, i to često **uz Kupu**. Tijekom tih šetnji moli **krunicu**. Ali molitvu često prekine netko tko ga pozdravi i pita kako je. *Sada ga već svi u Sisku poznaju*, kaže, iako ga prije nisu prepoznavali. Zato je znao birati stranu na kojoj nema mnogo ljudi: ne prema centru, nego dolje prema mostu. To ga veseli, kaže, i to bi volio nastaviti, *ako Bog da i dok Bog da*.
sections.subtitle_en: Guitar, matches, and the Rosary by the Kupa
sections.screenshot_description_en: Bishop Košić smilingly talks about walks by the Kupa with a Rosary in hand
sections.content_en:
When asked about talents, the bishop mentions **music**. He now sings mainly at Holy Masses, in the liturgy. He still takes up the guitar sometimes, but less and less frequently. He used to sing in company or in a relaxed atmosphere, but now, he admits, he does not have much time for that.

He also loved **sports, football, and basketball**, but today he mostly only watches matches. With a smile, he adds that *he is not at an age* when he could actively engage in sports.

Most of all he loves **walks**, and often **by the Kupa**. During those walks he prays the **Rosary**. But the prayer is often interrupted by someone greeting him and asking how he is. *Now everyone in Sisak already knows him*, he says, although before they did not recognize him. That is why he used to choose the side where there are not many people: not toward the center, but down toward the bridge. That brings him joy, he says, and he would like to continue that, *if God wills and as long as God wills*.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: Sisak ili Zagreb?
sections.screenshot_description: Biskup odgovara na blic pitanje Sisak ili Zagreb
sections.content:
Pred kraj razgovora voditelj najavljuje **blic pitanja** po načelu „ili-ili“. Ispričava se što ih nije unaprijed najavio i napominje da će neka biti *možda malo provokativna, ali ne i zlonamjerna*. Biskup se našali da *ne mora odgovoriti*, a voditelj odgovara da će se već dogovoriti.

Prvo pitanje glasi: **Sisak ili Zagreb?** Biskup odgovara diplomatski i temeljito. Zagreb je glavni grad Hrvatske i metropola koju ne može odbaciti jer je u njoj služio. Kada je došao u Sisak, imao je pedeset godina, a od toga je **više od 25 provelo u Zagrebu**. Nabraja i ostale postaje: rodni varaždinski kraj, vojsku, Karlovac, župničku službu u **Hrastovici** i **Petrinji**. Zatim navodi zagrebačke godine: školovanje, kapelaniju u **Španskom**, fakultet i službu pomoćnog biskupa. Zbrojeno, više je godina proveo u Zagrebu nego izvan njega.

Ipak, presuda je jasna: **„Sad sam u Sisku i to mi je najdraži grad.“** Voditelj dodaje da se ne mora odreći Zagreba, a biskup napominje da je to trebalo malo protumačiti gledateljima, *da se ne uvrijede ljudi iz Zagreba*.
sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: Sisak or Zagreb?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The bishop answers the quick-fire question Sisak or Zagreb
sections.content_en:
Towards the end of the conversation, the host announces **quick-fire questions** on the "either-or" principle. He apologizes for not announcing them in advance and notes that some will be *perhaps a little provocative, but not malicious*. The bishop jokes that he *does not have to answer*, and the host replies that they will work it out.

The first question is: **Sisak or Zagreb?** The bishop answers diplomatically and thoroughly. Zagreb is the capital of Croatia and a metropolis he cannot reject because he served in it. When he came to Sisak, he was fifty years old, and of that **more than 25 was spent in Zagreb**. He also lists other stations: his native Varaždin region, the army, Karlovac, parish service in **Hrastovica** and **Petrinji**. Then he lists his Zagreb years: schooling, chaplaincy in **Špansko**, faculty, and the ministry of auxiliary bishop. In total, he spent more years in Zagreb than outside of it.

Still, the verdict is clear: **"Now I am in Sisak and that is my favorite city."** The host adds that he does not have to renounce Zagreb, and the bishop notes that this needed to be explained a little to the viewers, *so that the people from Zagreb do not take offense*.

sections.subtitle: Propovijed ili razgovor, crkva ili čovjek
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Košić naglašava da je obnova čovjeka važnija od obnove crkava
sections.content:
Sljedeće pitanje glasi: **propovijed ili neformalni razgovor s vjernicima?** Biskup priznaje da je sada gotovo neprestano u prvoj ulozi, ali da mu je **draža neformalna komunikacija**. Tada može objasniti svoje stavove i vjeru te čuti pitanja, što je *ljepše nego samo odozgora*. Propovijed je ipak liturgijski čin u kojem nema mjesta dijalogu. Njegova je obveza **protumačiti riječ Božju**, primijeniti je na sadašnji trenutak i dati poruku.

Posljednje pitanje posebno je važno za biskupa koji upravo obnavlja desetke crkava nakon potresa: **obnova crkve ili obnova čovjeka?** Odgovor je nedvosmislen: **obnova čovjeka sigurno je važnija**, što je, kaže, rekao već više puta. Crkve se mogu obnoviti *u zlatu i srebru*, ali upozorava na dvije opasnosti:

- da **ljudi nestanu**, što se, nažalost, već dogodilo jer su mnogi nakon potresa otišli iz kraja,
- da **ljudi postanu ruševine**, što smatra najgorim i nečim što se ne bi smjelo dogoditi.

Zato se, kaže, svi bore pomoći svakom čovjeku koji je u problemima, koji se muči i *trga*. Zaključuje: **apsolutni je prioritet čovjek**.
sections.subtitle_en: Homily or conversation, church or man
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mons. Košić emphasizes that the renewal of man is more important than the renewal of churches
sections.content_en:
The next question reads: **homily or informal conversation with the faithful?** The bishop admits that he is now almost constantly in the first role, but that **informal communication is dearer to him**. Then he can explain his views and faith and hear questions, which is *nicer than just from above*. A homily is nevertheless a liturgical act in which there is no place for dialogue. His obligation is to **interpret the word of God**, apply it to the present moment, and give a message.

The last question is especially important for a bishop who is currently rebuilding dozens of churches after the earthquake: **renewal of the church or renewal of man?** The answer is unequivocal: **the renewal of man is certainly more important**, which, he says, he has already said several times. Churches can be renewed *in gold and silver*, but he warns of two dangers:

- that **people disappear**, which, unfortunately, has already happened because many left the region after the earthquake,
- that **people become ruins**, which he considers the worst and something that should not happen.

That is why, he says, everyone is fighting to help every person who is in trouble, who is struggling and *torn apart*. He concludes: **the absolute priority is man**.

sections.subtitle: Biskupov blagoslov za kraj i najava razgovora o evolucijskoj psihologiji
sections.screenshot_description: Mons. Vlado Košić podjeljuje blagoslov studiju, udruzi i gledateljima
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje biskupu od srca na sudjelovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je *mnogima progovorio*. Za kraj ga moli za **blagoslov studija, udruge i svih gledatelja**. Mons. Košić blagoslov podjeljuje liturgijskim obrascem: „Gospodin s vama.“ Slijede zazivi „Budi ime Gospodnje blagoslovljeno“ i „Pomoć je naša u imenu Gospodina“, na koje voditelj odgovara. Biskup završava riječima: **„Blagoslovio vas i sve vaše svemogući Bog, Otac i Sin i Duh Sveti.“**

Voditelj se zatim odjavljuje i poziva gledatelje da lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se na kanal te da, koliko mogu, podupru rad podcasta. Najavljuje da je sljedeća epizoda **Redefinicije** već dostupna preko **Patreon** profila.

Za kraj slijedi kratki isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornica, **evolucijska biologinja**, govori o **evolucijskoj psihologiji**. Smatra je važnom, ali u tom području vidi *veliko neznanje*. Najviše ju je, kaže, šokiralo kada je proučila predmete na studiju psihologije: na njemu ima *jako malo biologije*.
sections.subtitle_en: The Bishop's Blessing to Conclude and Announcement of a Conversation on Evolutionary Psychology
sections.screenshot_description_en: Mons. Vlado Košić imparts a blessing to the studio, the association, and the viewers
sections.content_en:
The host thanks the bishop from the heart for his participation and expresses the conviction that he *spoke to many*. In conclusion, he asks him for a **blessing for the studio, the association, and all the viewers**. Mons. Košić imparts the blessing using the liturgical formula: “The Lord be with you.” The invocations “Blessed be the name of the Lord” and “Our help is in the name of the Lord” follow, to which the host responds. The bishop concludes with the words: **“May almighty God bless you and all of yours, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit.”**

The host then signs off and invites the viewers to like, share, and subscribe to the channel, and to support the work of the podcast as much as they can. He announces that the next episode of **Redefinicija** is already available via the **Patreon** profile.

Finally, a short clip from the next episode follows. The interlocutor, an **evolutionary biologist**, speaks about **evolutionary psychology**. She considers it important, but sees *great ignorance* in that field. What shocked her the most, she says, was when she examined the courses in psychology studies: there is *very little biology* in it.
